tb-105-1.question:
Marcus finds it easier to walk on snow with snowshoes (Fig a). Without snowshoes, his feet sink into the snow (Fig b).

Which of the following best explains why snowshoes can help him walk on snow?

A The area of contact between the snowshoes and the snow is larger than that of ordinary shoes.

B Snowshoes exert a smaller force on the snow.

C Snowshoes exert a higher pressure on the snow.

D Snowshoes have a smoother contact surface with the snow.
tb-105-1.reasoning:
Pressure is p=F/A. The supporting force is still approximately the person's weight, but snowshoes spread it over a larger contact area, reducing pressure on the snow.

The snow is less likely to give way, making walking easier. The reason is the increased area, not a reduction in weight or an increase in pressure: A.

tb-105-2.question:
A gas satisfies the equation pV=13Nmc2¯. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The gas has NNA moles of molecules.

(2) Every molecule moves at the same speed c.

(3) The mass of the gas is Nm.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-105-2.reasoning:
N is the number of molecules and Nₐ is Avogadro's constant, so the amount is N/Nₐ mol. With mass m per molecule, the total gas mass is Nm. Statements (1) and (3) are correct.

The overbar on c² denotes a mean square speed, not a common speed of every molecule. Molecules have a distribution of speeds, so (2) is false. Choose B.

tb-105-4.question:
A helium balloon deflates after a few days (Fig c).

Which of the following statements about the deflated balloon is/are correct?

(1) The pressure of the helium gas is smaller than the air pressure outside the balloon.

(2) The helium gas does not fill up all the space inside the balloon.

(3) The volume of the balloon will increase if the air pressure outside the balloon decreases.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-105-4.reasoning:
A gas fills all available space, so the remaining helium still fills the balloon: (2) is false. At equilibrium its pressure balances external pressure and the rubber's inward elastic effect; it is not lower than external pressure, so (1) is false.

Reducing external pressure allows the gas to expand until a new equilibrium is reached. Only (3) is correct: B.

tb-105-6.question:
Two identical containers (Fig d) hold two ideal gases X and Y at the same temperature. Which of the following quantities must be the same for the two gases?

A The total molecular kinetic energy

B The r.m.s. speed of the molecules

C The average molecular kinetic energy

D The total mass of the gas
tb-105-6.reasoning:
The total mass of the two gases may not be the same.

As T ∝ KEaverage, the average molecular kinetic energy of the two gases must be the same.

As the number of molecules N in the two gases may not be the same, the total molecular kinetic energy (N × KEaverage) of the two gases may not be the same.

By 12mc2̅ = 3RT2NA,

crms = c2̅ = 3RTmNA

As the mass m of each gas molecule of the two gases may not be the same, crms of the two gases may not be the same.

tb-105-9.question:
(For Q9−10.) The pressure of an ideal gas at state M is increased at a constant volume and then expands at a constant pressure to state N (Fig f ). Given: 1 atm = 105 Pa

C 1.95 × 106 J

tb-105-9.reasoning:
Internal energy

= N × 12mc2̅

= 32 × 13Nmc2̅

= 32 × pV

Change in internal energy

= 32 × (pNVN − pMVM)

= 32 × (1.3 × 105 × 10 − 0.8 × 105 × 2)

= 1.71 × 106 J

tb-105-11.question:
Figure g shows two containers made of conducting walls. One of the containers is filled with ideal gas X and the other is filled with ideal gas Y. Which of the following statements is/are correct after a long period of time?

(1) The root-mean-square speeds of the molecules of the two gases will become the same even if their molar masses are not the same.

(2) The total kinetic energies of the two gases will become the same even if their masses are not the same.

(3) The average kinetic energies of the molecules of the two gases will become the same even if their number of moles are not the same.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-105-11.reasoning:
The temperature T of the two gases will become the same after a long period of time.

As T ∝ KEaverage, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of the two gases will become the same.

∴ (3) is correct.

If the masses of the two gases are not the same, the number of molecules N in the two gases may not be the same. As a result, the total kinetic energy (N × KEaverage) of the two gases may not become the same.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

By 12mc2̅ = 3RT2NA,

crms = c2̅ = 3RTmNA

If the molar mass mNA of the two gases are not the same, crms of the two gases will not become the same.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

n = pVRT 1M

= (105×103)×58.31×(27+273)
